_meta.indication: Indicated to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and heart failure (HF) hospitalization following a hospitalization for heart failure or need for outpatient IV diuretics, in adults with symptomatic chronic HF and ejection fraction less than 45%.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: VICTORIA (VerICiguaT GlObal Study in Subjects With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection FrAction)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, double-blind, event-driven, multi-center trial comparing vericiguat (up to 10 mg daily, started at 2.5 mg once daily and doubled every 2 weeks to the target maintenance dose) to matching placebo on a background of standard of care HF therapies; subjects randomized 1:1.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with chronic HF (NYHA Class II-IV) and reduced ejection fraction (LVEF < 45%), elevated natriuretic peptides, and a previous HF decompensation (defined as HF hospitalization within 6 months before randomization or use of IV diuretics for HF within 3 months before randomization).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to the first occurrence of the composite of CV death or HF hospitalization.
pivotal_trials.result: Primary composite endpoint (CV death or HF hospitalization) occurred in 897 (35.5%) vericiguat vs 972 (38.5%) placebo; HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.82, 0.98); p=0.019, with a 4.2% annualized absolute risk reduction.

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of Vericiguat in Participants With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) (MK-1242-001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were hypotension (16% vericiguat vs 15% placebo) and anemia (10% vs 7%). Principal adverse drug reactions of interest were symptomatic hypotension, syncope, and anemia (each ~4% annual likelihood).
target_moa: Vericiguat is a stimulator of soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), an enzyme in the nitric oxide (NO) signaling pathway; sGC stimulation increases intracellular cGMP, a signaling molecule involved in vascular smooth muscle relaxation, cardiac contractility, and cardiac remodeling.
modality: Small molecule (oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — Do not administer VERQUVO to a pregnant female because it may cause fetal harm; exclude pregnancy before treatment and use effective contraception during treatment and for one month after stopping.

rems.type: The Division of Risk Management and the Division of Cardiology and Nephrology determined that a REMS is not needed to ensure the benefits of vericiguat outweigh its risks; the risk of embryo-fetal toxicity is communicated through labeling.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened; the study design, endpoints, and statistical plan were typical and results clear and non-controversial.

summary.text: Vericiguat received fast track designation in 2014 under IND 116743 for HFrEF; the NDA (submitted May 2020) was granted priority review status on July 14, 2020 and was approved first-cycle without an advisory committee based on the single Phase 3 VICTORIA trial.

citations.quote: Vericiguat received fast track designation in 2014 under its IND 116743 for the treatment of HFrEF and this NDA application received priority review status on July 14, 2020.
The NDA was submitted in May 2020 and was granted priority review status.
The primary evidence of effectiveness is from one Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, event-driven, multicenter clinical trial (VICTORIA)
An advisory committee meeting was not convened to discuss this application.
